key_insight: Sr2+ doping in Nd2-xSrxCoMnO6-δ drives a structural and magnetic crossover that enables control of normal versus inverse exchange bias.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how composition tuning can be used to engineer exchange-bias strength and sign in rare-earth double perovskites for magnetic device design.
method: Neutron powder diffraction to track B-site order and phase evolution
X-ray absorption spectroscopy to follow Co/Mn valence changes
DC magnetization and AC susceptibility to probe ferromagnetism, glassiness, and exchange bias
evidence_signal: The strongest reported result is a ~4 kOe exchange-bias field at 8 K for x = 0.75 under a 6 T cooling field, with robust inverse EB persisting after minor-loop correction.
watch_item: The observed exchange bias is closely tied to low-temperature, composition-specific magnetic disorder, so reproducibility and minor-loop correction are critical when translating this behavior into applications.
paper_title: Antisite-disorder driven tuning of magnetic properties and exchange-bias in Nd$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$CoMnO$_{6-δ}$ $(0 \leq x \leq 1)$ ($δ\sim 0.5$) double perovskites
